sections.heading: Identity and current status
sections.body:
- Project ID: `aider`
- Canonical name: Aider (`claim-aider-w2-identity`)
- Current status: dormant. The repository is not archived (`claim-aider-w2-status`). Latest GitHub release remains v0.86.0 (2025-08-09); the maintainer said on 2025-10-30 he was occupied with other projects; PyPI later published 0.86.2 on 2026-02-12 (`claim-aider-sf-dormant-2026-08-15`, `claim-aider-w2-version-conflict`, `claim-aider-w2-version-tags`, `claim-aider-w2-version-package`).
- Last source-backed identity check: 2026-08-10

sections.heading: What it is and is not
sections.body:
- What it is: a local terminal pair-programming runtime with repository-map, file, Git, and provider integrations (`claim-aider-w2-primary-type`, `claim-aider-w2-unique`).
- What it is not: checked evidence does not establish a hosted remote agent, native mobile client, messaging gateway, vendor relay, scheduler, or parallel agent system (`claim-aider-w2-not-for`).

sections.heading: Architecture and agent-loop ownership
sections.body:
- Primary type: `runtime` (`claim-aider-w2-primary-type`)
- Agent-loop owner: Aider's Coder assembles context, calls the configured model, applies edits, runs approved local actions, and records Git changes (`claim-aider-w2-loop-owner`).
- Architecture: local process against a repository, with optional Docker or GitHub Codespaces host routes (`claim-aider-w2-execution`, `claim-aider-w2-optional-docker`, `claim-aider-w2-surface-codespaces`).

sections.heading: Surfaces and execution location
sections.body:
- Surface IDs: `surface-aider-cli`, `surface-aider-voice-cli`, `surface-aider-browser-ui`, `surface-aider-ide-watch`, `surface-aider-python-api`, `surface-aider-docker-cli`, `surface-aider-codespaces`.
- Execution location: local host by default; optional same-device Docker container; GitHub-managed Codespaces terminal (`claim-aider-w2-execution`, `claim-aider-w2-optional-docker`, `claim-aider-w2-surface-codespaces`).

sections.heading: Model/auth/provider strategy
sections.body:
- Model strategy: main, weak, and editor models; aliases; in-chat switching; reasoning-effort and thinking-token controls (`claim-aider-w2-model-strategy`). The weak model is not established as fallback.
- Auth strategy: user-supplied provider credentials (`claim-aider-w2-provider-auth`).
- Provider support: LiteLLM, OpenAI-compatible endpoints, OpenAI, Anthropic, Ollama, and other documented providers (`claim-aider-w2-provider-auth`).

sections.heading: Context, memory, compaction, and session behavior
sections.body:
- Context behavior: ranked repository map, local history, context controls, and selected file content (`claim-aider-w2-context-session`).
- Memory: local session-history restoration is supported; a separate project-memory service remains unknown (`claim-aider-w2-context-session`).
- Compaction: ChatSummary compaction is included in the context/session claim (`claim-aider-w2-context-session`).
- Session behavior: local history files and optional restore; cross-machine resume remains unknown (`claim-aider-w2-context-session`, `claim-aider-w2-not-for`).

sections.heading: Tools, extensions, MCP, skills, hooks, and APIs
sections.body:
- Tools: files, repository map, Git, shell, tests, lint, web scrape, image input, voice, diff, undo, watch, and scripting (`claim-aider-w2-tools-api`).
- Extensions: no separate first-party extension framework was established beyond watch mode, configuration, and scripting; `unknown`.
- MCP: `unknown`.
- Skills: `unknown`.
- Hooks: lifecycle hooks are `unknown`; Git pre-commit verification is a separate documented control.
- APIs: one-shot CLI scripting and a local Python Coder API (`claim-aider-w2-surface-api`, `claim-aider-w2-tools-api`).

sections.heading: Orchestration and parallelism
sections.body:
- Orchestration: Architect mode is a sequential architect request followed by an editor request (`claim-aider-w2-orchestration`).
- Parallelism: subagents, agent teams, and parallel workers remain unknown (`claim-aider-w2-not-for`).

sections.heading: Isolation, permissions, security, and data path
sections.body:
- Isolation: no default built-in sandbox was established; optional Docker maps the repository into a container (`claim-aider-w2-optional-docker`).
- Permissions: shell work and edits to files outside the chat set use confirmation paths; dry-run and Git controls are available (`claim-aider-w2-security-data`).
- Security: no formal Aider security audit, threat model, or repository security policy was established.
- Data path: Aider assembles repository and chat context locally and sends it to the configured LiteLLM endpoint; provider retention remains provider-specific (`claim-aider-w2-security-data`).

sections.heading: Interface inventory plus remote/mobile/background behavior
sections.body:
- Interface and surface IDs:
  - Terminal: `surface-aider-cli`, `surface-aider-voice-cli` (`claim-aider-w2-surface-cli-voice`).
  - Browser: `surface-aider-browser-ui` (`claim-aider-w2-surface-browser`).
  - IDE watch: `surface-aider-ide-watch` (`claim-aider-w2-surface-watch`).
  - API: `surface-aider-python-api` (`claim-aider-w2-surface-api`).
  - Optional hosts: `surface-aider-docker-cli`, `surface-aider-codespaces` (`claim-aider-w2-optional-docker`, `claim-aider-w2-surface-codespaces`).
- Remote behavior: remote start, cross-machine resume, first-party remote client, and vendor relay remain unknown (`claim-aider-w2-not-for`). Generic SSH is not treated as a native Aider surface.
- Mobile behavior: native iOS/Android, mobile web, messaging, and Termux guidance remain unknown (`claim-aider-w2-not-for`). Voice input is not a mobile route.
- Background behavior: scheduler, daemon, hosted worker, and issue-to-PR routes remain unknown (`claim-aider-w2-not-for`).

sections.heading: Pricing, license, maintenance, and lock-in
sections.body:
- Pricing: no Aider-owned subscription price was established; provider and Copilot costs are external (`claim-aider-w2-pricing`).
- License: Apache-2.0 (`claim-aider-w2-license`).
- Maintenance: repository active; version surfaces conflict (`claim-aider-w2-status`, `claim-aider-w2-version-conflict`, `claim-aider-w2-version-tags`, `claim-aider-w2-version-package`).
- Lock-in: open source and provider configuration are documented, but a formal lock-in analysis and complete cost matrix remain unknown (`claim-aider-w2-provider-auth`, `claim-aider-w2-lineage`).

sections.heading: Unique edge, meaningful drawbacks, best fit, and not-for
sections.body:
- Unique edge: terminal pair programming with a ranked repository map and direct local Git integration across broad providers (`claim-aider-w2-unique`).
- Meaningful drawbacks: weaker-model edit failures (`claim-aider-w2-drawback`) and an experimental browser UI (`claim-aider-w2-surface-browser`).
- Best fit: official guidance addresses developers who want local AI pair programming against a new or existing codebase, especially a local Git repository (`claim-aider-w2-intended-user`). This is not a recommendation.
- Not-for: verified native mobile, messaging, remote relay, hosted background, or parallel-agent needs remain outside the established surface set (`claim-aider-w2-not-for`).
